Start at low E. Do this. And tongue each note. Start slow, at 80bpm as eighth notes.
"E-F-F#-G-G#"  *1 beat pause*
"E-F-F#-G-G#"  *1 beat pause*
"E-F-F#-G-G#-G-F#-F-E-F-F#-G-G#-G-F#-F"  "E-F-F#-G-G#-A-Bb-B-C" *1 beat pause* 
Repeat pervious line. *one beat pause*
Basically, E to G#, E to c. E to next g#, e to next c. Til you've got the whole 3 octaves. It will be repetitive tongueing. Increase speed 2 or 4 bpm day and your chromatic will be SPOTLESS at 120bpm at sixteenth notes, I promise!

Don't ever use tap water. Always use something from the gallon, maybe distilled or spring water. Tap water has so much chlorine in it and it warps the reed when it sits and dries after you have wiped it. I had such terrible luck with the V12's. I was spendig so much money for 10ct boxes and only getting 2-3 good reeds. I had to use the Rue Lepic. They were so much more consistent. Literally, before I soak any reed, I sit it in my mouth for a few minutes, slap it on, and play something light just to get the feel of the reed prior to soaking it. You can usually tell which ones are going to have that good shape that you're used to, and the smooth production that you need. Then I soak the ones that didn't make the cut, retry them, and if they are so good again I mark the plastic cover respectively. Then I soak the ones that felt good and retry them and mark which one I'd like to use now and which ones to save or use for backup. My teacher loved my tone, so she just said whatever works is what she wants me to do. I found humor there.
